findings.claim: New namespace import `* as regexes from "../core/regexes.js"` may be unused, duplicate an existing `core.regexes` access path, or shadow/collide with a local identifier named `regexes` later in this large file.
findings.rationale: The hunk only adds the import; the usage site is not shown. Zod's core index typically re-exports regexes (accessible as `core.regexes`), so importing the module directly can create a second module specifier for the same code and, under bundler/circular-import conditions in the v4 core graph, a different initialization order. It also risks a name collision if `schemas.ts` already defines or destructures a `regexes` binding. Low confidence without the rest of the file — worth verifying that `regexes.` is actually referenced, that no other `regexes` identifier exists in scope, and that `core.regexes` wouldn't be the consistent access pattern. If unused, most lint/TS `noUnusedLocals` configs would flag it and it would still be emitted as a side-effectful import by some bundlers.
